newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Highlands Pacific lists at A$1.00.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Highlands Pacific lists at A$1.00.

text.p: Shares in Papua New Guinea (PNG) base metals and gold explorer Highlands Pacific Ltd listed on the Australian Stock Exchange on Thursday at the issue price of A$1.00 each, and moved within a tight range of A$1.00 and A$1.05 in early trade.

The company plans to develop its Ramu nickel/cobalt and Freida River copper/gold projects in PNG, while continuing exploration work on mineral deposits in other parts of the South Pacific nation and Indonesia.
Highlands Pacific raised A$190 million from the issue of a similar number of shares.

The company's chief executive, Ian Holzberger, said in late April that a decision on the developement of Ramu was expected by the end of 1998 and the company hoped to find a partner for the Freida project by the end of 1997.
Highlands Pacific was born from a restructure proposal put forward by Highlands Gold Ltd after a successful takeover offer by Canadian miner Placer Dome Inc late last year.

The bulk of the funds raised in the float were used to acquire the exploration assets from Placer, which wanted the 25 percent stake in the giant Porgera gold mine in PNG and was willing to offload the other assets.
The Freida resource was estimated to contain 4.8 million tonnes of copper and 9.1 million ounces of gold.

A pre-feasibility study has estimated project capital costs of US$1.56 billion with an average annual production of 220,000 tonnes of copper cathode and 333,000 ounces of gold in the first 13 years of an expected mine life of 23 years.
The Ramu resource was estimated to contain 1.1 million tonnnes of nickel and 0.1 million tonnes of cobalt.

A pre-feasibility study had estimated project capital costs of US$764 million with an average annual production of 33,000 tonnes of nikel metal and 2,800 tonnes of cobalt salt over a total mine life of 20 years.
The third part of the company's strategy involved continued exploration in PNG and Indonesia with A$18 million of funds earmarked for this over the next three years.
Highland Pacific offered about 76.5 million shares to investors and institutions as part of its plan to raise A$190 million.
Five PNG institutions control the company with a combined stake of more than 51 percent.
By 11.10 a.m. (0110 GMT), Highlands Pacific shares had settled to A$1.01.
